name: Mount Misen (弥山) on Miyajima, Daisho-in course
region: Seto Inland Sea National Park, Hiroshima
why: From the temple behind the floating torii, hundreds of stone steps through protected primeval forest to granite boulders 535 m above the Seto Inland Sea.
book: Free, no permit. Ferries every 15 minutes from Miyajimaguchi; Daisho-in is a 30-minute walk from the pier. The summit observatory is open 10:00-16:00. To skip the descent, walk 20 minutes down to the Shishiiwa ropeway station (last car down 17:00-17:30).
water: No water or vending machines on the trail or at the summit; the nearest drinks are at the top ropeway station. Carry 1-1.5 litres; toilets at the summit.
dangers: Steep stone steps all the way: hard on the knees going down, slippery when wet.
Hornets and mamushi pit vipers live on the mountain: rare, but call 119 if stung or bitten.
Summer heat and humidity: start early in July and August.
Stay on the three official courses: other paths are broken by typhoons and people get lost every year.
turnaround: Not at the Misen Hondo halls by 14:30: go up to the summit only if you will take the ropeway down, before the last car.

points.name: Daisho-in temple
points.note: Miyajima's oldest temple, 600 m behind Itsukushima Shrine. The Daisho-in course starts at the signboard beside it: 2.5 km to the top.

points.name: Misen Hondo and Reikado
points.note: Temple halls below the summit where Kobo Daishi is said to have trained; in the Reikado a fire has been kept burning for some 1,200 years.

points.name: Misen summit rocks
points.note: 535 m: huge granite boulders and an open wooden observatory, with islands of the Inland Sea on every side and Hiroshima across the bay.
